title: Lee County School Board, District 4
what_it_does: School board members set the district budget and school-tax rate, hire the superintendent (where appointed), approve school boundaries, curriculum policy and construction, and set district policies. Nonpartisan.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); both candidates are marked Qualified, which for a nonpartisan seat means the August vote did not produce a majority winner (or the seat is decided only in November). Positions have not been researched; check the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Tony Beougher
candidates.background: Beougher is a Fort Myers High School graduate with an economics degree from Wake Forest University who works as a vice president of sales at the research firm Gartner. He is a father of six, a foster parent and a church leader active in youth mentoring. He led the District 4 field in fundraising with about $53,000 raised.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

education_choice.summary: Beougher's campaign priorities page says parents must have the freedom to choose their child's educational environment because every child learns differently, and expresses support for charter schools and competitive options.
education_choice.quote: Every child learns differently... parents must have the freedom to choose

school_safety.summary: His priorities page calls for strong discipline, enforcement of accountability and stronger school security, saying students cannot thrive amid chaos or fear. It does not mention counselors or mental-health staffing.
school_safety.quote: No student can thrive in an environment of chaos or fear.

taxes.summary: Beougher says tax dollars should go to classrooms rather than bureaucracy and emphasizes efficiency and cutting waste, and at a candidate forum stressed accountability and transparency; he has not proposed cutting taxes or the school millage.

other_issues.title: Parental rights and curriculum transparency
other_issues.summary: He pledges transparency in curriculum and says families should have a voice in decisions affecting their children, calling parents 'the first and most important teachers in a child's life.'

other_issues.title: Career and technical education
other_issues.summary: He supports expanding vocational programs and partnerships with local businesses.

candidates.name: Debbie Jordan
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Lee County School Board member, District 4
candidates.background: Jordan has represented District 4 on the Lee County School Board since 2019 and is seeking a third and final term. She is a longtime Lee County resident with children and grandchildren in district schools. The race takes place as the district absorbs a proposed $47 million budget reduction and declining enrollment, with about 475 employees, including 275 teachers, not offered renewed contracts.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

teacher_pay.summary: Jordan objected to how the district described staff reductions during its budget cuts and said problems should be addressed 'at the top' so schools keep the resources they need. She also said the district should use its own experienced teachers to train colleagues rather than pay outside trainers.
teacher_pay.quote: They consider them units. I consider them human beings with families.

sources.title: Four candidates vie for District 4 seat on Lee County School Board

education_choice.summary: Jordan promotes the district's career academies as an advantage public schools hold over private schools, framing them as a reason families should stay in the district rather than take their funding elsewhere.
education_choice.quote: In Lee County, the academies that we have in our schools, they don't have that in your private schools.

sources.title: Four candidates vie for District 4 seat on Lee County School Board

record.item: Elected to the Lee County School Board in 2018, taking office in 2019, and re-elected to a second term; currently seeking a third term.

sources.title: Four candidates vie for District 4 seat on Lee County School Board
